# Jig

> Jig turns plain-English automation requests into versioned TypeScript workflows. A single runtime engine executes deterministic code, with explicit `llm()` and `agent()` hatches and step-scoped typed MCP tools.

## Agent routing

- To install, set up, connect, deploy or update an instance, read `.agents/skills/jig/SKILL.md`.
- To write or edit a jig, read `SKILL.md` completely.
- To change the Jig runtime, API, scheduler, dashboard, database, or connection system, read `CLAUDE.md`.
- To deploy, diagnose, recover, or self-heal an instance, read `docs/operations.md`.
- For the product overview and architecture diagram, read `README.md`.
- For contribution and validation expectations, read `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

## Fast paths

### Run locally

```sh
bun install
bun run jig start
```

The dashboard opens on a loopback URL. Authorize OpenRouter when it asks (browser flow, no key to paste), connect the required services, then author and run jigs from the dashboard. `bun run jig setup` does the same walk from a terminal.

### Author a jig

```sh
bun run jig connect
bun run jig new "Every weekday at 8am, email me a concise briefing."
bun run jig edit <jig-id>
bun run jig run <jig-id> --dry-run
bun run jig run <jig-id>
```

`new`, `edit` and `run` act on the deployed instance in `~/.config/jig/remotes/` when one
exists, and on this machine otherwise; `--local` forces this machine and `--handle=<name>`
chooses between deployed instances. They print the target before starting. An unpaired remote
is an error rather than a silent fall back to local.

Every jig exports `jig(name, options, handler)` from `@jig/sdk`. Every logical unit of work belongs in a flat `ctx.step()` block. Direct code is preferred over `llm()`, and `llm()` is preferred over `agent()`. Connection tools must appear in the jig-level and current-step allowlists. Use `ctx.output()` for observable results.

The approved jig version in SQLite is authoritative — there is no jig source on disk. `jig run` and the dashboard both execute that version.

### Deploy

Use the Deploy on Railway button in `README.md` for a clean one-click installation, or run:

```sh
bun run jig deploy
```

The deployment must have a persistent volume mounted at `/data`; it holds the encrypted credentials, versioned jigs, schedules, and run history. No maintainer data or credentials belong in the template.

Update an existing linked deployment with:

```sh
bun run jig deploy --update
```

### Diagnose and heal

```sh
bun run jig doctor [handle]
bun run jig pair <code>          # code from the dashboard's Setup page; no password involved
# Or sign in with the instance password, kept out of shell history:
read -s JIG_PASSWORD && export JIG_PASSWORD
bun run jig unlock [handle]
unset JIG_PASSWORD
bun run jig run <jig-id> --dry-run
bun run jig debug tail [handle]
```

To edit a deployed jig outside the dashboard (pushes land pending unless `--approve`):

```sh
bun run jig debug connections    # what is connected, and how many tools each has
bun run jig debug ls [handle]
bun run jig edit <jig-id> --out=/tmp/<jig-id>.ts
bun run jig edit <jig-id> --file=/tmp/<jig-id>.ts --message="what changed"
```

To see what a connection's tool really returns before writing unwrap code:

```sh
bun run jig debug eval <server> <tool> --args='{"max_results":3}'
```

For workflow rollback and approval:

```sh
bun run jig versions <jig-id>
bun run jig restore <jig-id> <version>
bun run jig pending <jig-id>
bun run jig pending <jig-id> approve
bun run jig pending <jig-id> discard
```

For backup and disaster recovery:

The dashboard has the same thing under Settings > Backup: download a .zip, or
pick one to restore (choosing a file previews it; nothing changes until you
confirm). From the CLI:

```sh
bun run jig backup                              # writes jig-backup-<date>.zip
bun run jig backup --no-credentials             # shareable copy, secrets omitted
bun run jig backup restore <file.zip> --dry-run # print the plan, change nothing
bun run jig backup restore <file.zip>
```

The archive carries jigs and their active code, schedules, connections (custom
servers, tool permissions, MCP schemas), settings and jig memory. Credentials
travel as ciphertext with the salt they need, so restoring them requires the
same password the backup was made under; onto an instance with a different
password they are skipped unless `--force` is passed. Run history, logs and
step caches are deliberately not included.

After two consecutive real-run failures, Jig can start a repair authoring session. The proposed patch remains pending and never ships without approval. If AgentMail is configured, the owner receives a reply-to-approve thread; otherwise the proposal remains visible in the dashboard.

## Safety invariants

- Never commit `.env`, `.jig/`, `jig.db*`, `jig.log`, `runtime/`, `tmp/`, credentials, tokens, OAuth state, personal information, or client data.
- Never print secrets while debugging. Use redacted structured logs and the dashboard.
- Never edit SQLite directly to change a jig. Use authoring, pending approval, restore, or the store APIs.
- Never deploy without `/data` persistence. A redeploy without the volume loses credentials, jigs, schedules, and history.
- Never auto-approve an AI-generated repair.
- Before publishing, run relevant tests, `git diff --check`, and a tracked-file privacy/secret scan.

## Validation

```sh
bun test
git diff --check
```

For a narrow change, run the closest test file first, then the full suite when runtime, scheduler, database, connection, authoring, or deployment behavior changed.
